correctness.rationale: For ordered u<v, F=(v-u)sqrt(1+(u+v)^2) strictly increases in the difference at fixed sum, ruling out interior maxima. Reflection reduces the edges to (2a-w)sqrt(1+w²). The derivative has the sign of 2aw-2w²-1, including the stationary nonmaximum at the double root. The larger root gives the unique interior edge maximum and F²-4a²=w⁴-w²-1 there, so w²=φ is the only tie and its reflected pair is distinct. At the corner the local deficit is ξ+η+O((ξ+η)²). At the other contacts, differentiating the distance (not squared distance) gives ∂vF=2sqrt(1+w²) and -∂uuF/2=(2w²-1)/(2w sqrt(1+w²)). The repaired proof bounds the remainder by half the linear–quadratic loss on sufficiently small neighborhoods; compactness excludes other regions, and the rescaled indicators converge in L1 with Jacobians ε² and ε^(3/2)/(A sqrt(B)). Multiplying areas 1/2 and 4/3 by the ordered density 1/(2a²), with two reflected contacts in the latter case, gives both constants and the conditional total variation limits. At equality the corner is lower order. The original's no-atom argument at D alone did not justify equality of strict and weak tails at D−ε; the replacement proves atomlessness at every level via the nonzero quartic in v and Fubini. The frozen checker was inspected, not run; finite grid and quadrature are ancillary.
